newsitem.title: USA: Micron profit rose 66 percent in 3rd quarter.
newsitem.headline: Micron profit rose 66 percent in 3rd quarter.

text.p: Micron Technology Inc. said Monday its earnings rose a better-than-expected 66 percent for the latest quarter, boosted by higher prices for its computer memory chips.

Micron, based in Boise, Idaho, said net income jumped to $96.8 million, or 44 cents a share, for its third quarter ended on June 16, from $58.2 million, or 27 cents, a year earlier. Sales rose 25 percent to $965 million from $771 million.
Wall Street expected Micron to earn 38 cents a share, according to Zacks Investment Research, which tracks analysts' estimates.
Micron, one of the world's largest makers of computer memory chips, said profits improved as it got better at producing a new generation of chips using more advanced technology.
Micron also makes personal computers. PC sales rose 29 percent to $361.8 million in the third quarter from $280.3 million a year ago.

Gross margins on semiconductor products rose to 49 percent in the third quarter compared with 32 percent in the second quarter and 38 percent in the year-ago quarter. Gross margins is a measure of how much the company earns for each dollar of products sold.
The company also benefitted from an increase in prices for dynamic random-access memory chips.

But Micron said falling PC prices and customers' preferences for Micron's low-priced PC products hurt gross margins in its PC business. The third-quarter PC gross margin was 15 percent, down from 17 percent in the second quarter and 16 percent in last year's third quarter.
Micron said it continues to see pressure on its PC gross margins as competitors cut prices.
Micron released its earnings after the market had closed. Its shares had risen $1.75 to $42.50, partly in anticipation of a good quarter, analysts said.
